Apps to download before you fly to Korea 📲

Naver Map, not Google: Google Maps still can't give turn-by-turn directions here.
k.ride or Uber for taxis, both take foreign cards.
Baemin for delivery, in English now.
Papago for menus and signs.

Feeling rough on your Korea trip? 💊

Most everyday medicine is sold over the counter at a 약국 (yakguk, pharmacy). Just say the symptom:
두통 (dutong) headache
열이 나요 (yeori nayo) I have a fever
목이 아파요 (mogi apayo) sore throat
배탈 (baetal) upset stomach

Save this, you'll thank yourself later 📌
More phrases and what to buy: link in bio

Cash or card in Korea? 💳

Foreign Visa and Mastercard work almost everywhere. Always choose to pay in KRW.
Keep some cash for markets, street food and topping up T-money.
Use ATMs marked "Global ATM", about ₩3,500–5,000 a withdrawal.
No tipping, anywhere.

Save this before your trip 📌
Prepaid cards and the cheapest options: link in bio

Got sick in Korea? Seeing a doctor is easier than you think 🏥

Walk into a neighbourhood clinic (의원, uiwon) with your passport. No appointment needed.
The standard first visit is ₩18,840 in 2026. With medicine, roughly ₩20,000–40,000.
You get a prescription and buy the medicine at the pharmacy next door.

Save this, just in case 📌
English-speaking clinics and costs: link in bio

Checked out but your flight's tonight? 🧳

Subway lockers (T-Locker) in 273 stations, from ₩2,200 for 4 hours.
Staffed counters at Seoul Station, Myeongdong and Hongik Univ., from ₩3,000.
Or send your bags straight to Incheon from about ₩20,000–30,000. Book a day ahead.

Save this for your last day 📌
All the options and prices: link in bio

Lost your phone, wallet or passport in Korea? It's probably coming back 🙏

Check Lost112 first: the police's national lost and found, with an English section.
On the subway, tell station staff the time, platform and car right away.
In a taxi you paid by card? T-money can trace it: 1644-1188.

Save this, hopefully you never need it 📌
What to do step by step: link in bio

You have three ages in Korea, and all three are correct 🎂

International age: your passport, official since 2023.
Korean age: +1 at birth, +1 every 1 January.
Year age: still used for alcohol and military service.

Which one do you tell people at the bar? 👇
